title: 5 years of heartbreak: Mother still grieves son killed in Ruston - NewsBreak
text:
RUSTON, La. (KTVE/KARD) — For one local mother, July 7, 2020, marks a heartbreaking milestone. It’s the day her oldest son was shot and killed. To this day, the person responsible has not been identified, and the case remains unsolved. “Antonio was a genuine, kindhearted person, funny, goofy person. You know? He was well loved, and to know him was to love him”, said Alishia Robinson as she reflected on the kind of person her son was before his life was tragically cut short. According to the Ruston Police Department, Antonio “Kut” Robinson was shot and killed in a shooting that happened on the North Service Road, just west of Hwy 167. So far, authorities have not released any additional details about the incident. For the past five years, Alishia and her family have been waiting for justice. She shares what life has felt like without her son: “empty… It’s like I have a hole in my heart. I’m used to him coming in the house, talking his noise, being goofy, being silly, getting on my nerves at times, or whatever. It’s like empty. I have a hole in my heart that can never be filled”. Antonio had recently become a father, and at the time of his death, his daughter was only eight months old. “But his baby girl, she brings me joy when she’s around”, Alishia explains. Although there is joy, she is left to answer some pretty tough questions from her granddaughter, now age five. “Who killed my daddy? Ain’t nothing I can answer, you know, I don’t know what to say”, she added. Although words may be few when asked a question like that, Alishia does have a message for the person responsible for her son’s death. God sits high and he look low. Ya’ll day is coming and I’m have faith. I’m not giving up, so ya’ll might as well turn yourself in. I just want to see you face to face and just ask you like what did my son really do to you? Ya’ll are some cowards, ya’ll are some cowards, because you really didn’t have to shoot my baby in the back And to the detectives on the case: “I love the detectives on the case, but I feel like they should work harder. They should be doing more”, said Alishia. Got a tip? Call Crime Stoppers at 318-388-CASH. Antonio’s mother went on to say she’ll never lose her faith, and she feels like justice is just around the corner.
